transcript: It is a season of celebrities in great plays on Broadway, and a hot new bombshell has entered the villa. Mother Play, starring Jessica Lange, Celia Keenan-Bolger, and Jim Parsons, is a new piece by Paula Vogel about a mother raising her two children after having separated from her husband. As much as it seems that she wants to love and care for her kids, Phyllis, played by Jessica Lange, really struggles and at times her struggles are insurmountable. She struggles to put food on the table, she struggles to guide her children, and she struggles to accept who they are. Through decades of trials and tribulations, and a very small handful of good memories, her children Martha and Carl keep her and one another afloat. The close relationship that Martha and Carl have together is really beautiful, but it's bittersweet since you kind of know that it has only blossomed this much in the face of needing to survive. The performances in this play are incredible, and nuanced, and feel, for lack of a better term, very real. I thought this was kind of a hard watch, and I think it could be very hard hitting for anyone who has or has had a tumultuous relationship with their parents. But, I would recommend it nonetheless. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
